```{r}

library(growthcurver)

# Read in the Data
data <- read.csv(file='[FILE NAME.csv]', header = TRUE)

#Enter Constants Here (Time Increment is in Minutes)
time_increment <- 
total_hours <- 
  
#Initializing the new time array, and a pH range list 
tminutes <- (total_hours*60/time_increment) + 1
data$Time <- (1:tminutes)*time_increment
pH_list <- seq(3.2, 7.7, 0.3)


#Input Strain #1 (Columns 1 and 2) Name in the Quotation Marks
strain1_name <- ""

#Input Strain #2 (Columns 3 and 4) Name in the Quotation Marks
strain2_name <- ""

#Blanks (Columns 5 and 6) 
blanks <- "blank"

#Input Strain #3 (Columns 7 and 8) Name in the Quotation Marks
strain3_name <- ""

#Input Strain #4 (Columns 9 and 10) Name in the Quotation Marks
strain4_name <- ""

#Input Strain #5 (Columns 11 and 12) Name in the Quotation Marks
strain5_name <- ""

strain_list <- c(strain1_name, strain2_name, "blank", strain3_name, strain4_name, strain5_name)

for (j in 1:6){
  if(j == 3){  
}
  else{
    #This plots the 16 different pHs for the Given Strain with Peptone ([STRAIN] + P). Also scales the graph so that it's decently visible. 
    plot(0,0, type = "l", xlab = "Time (Minutes)", ylim = c(0, 1), xlim = c(0, tminutes*time_increment + 100), ylab = "Optical Density", main = strain_list[j])
    
    #Initialization of empty list that aims to contain the growth rates
    grate_list <- list()
    
    #Takes three entries in a row for that strain, which have pH differences of 2.4. The loop iterates through all 8 rows (hence the + 12*i), and then puts it into growthcurver to fit the data. It then puts those values into the grate_list, which is an array with the growth rates for that strain that lines up with the pH_list (which is just a list with the pH range, using steps of 0.3). It also graphs the line of the OD curve onto the main plot.
    for(i in 0:7){
      lines(data$Time, data[,2*j+1+12*i], col=c(i+1))
      gc_fit <- SummarizeGrowth(data$Time, data[,2*j+1+12*i])
      grate_list[i+1] <- gc_fit$vals$r
      
      lines(data$Time, data[,2*j+2+12*i], col=c(i+9))
      gc_fit2 <- SummarizeGrowth(data$Time, data[,2*j+2+12*i])
      grate_list[i+9]=gc_fit2$vals$r
      
    }
    legend("topleft", legend = c("pH 3.2", "pH 3.5", "pH 3.8", "pH 4.1", "pH 4.4", "pH 4.7", "pH 5.0", "pH 5.3", "pH 5.6", "pH 5.9", "pH 6.2", "pH 6.5", "pH 6.8", "pH 7.1", "pH 7.4", "pH 7.7"), col = (1:17), lty = 1, cex = 0.5)
    
    #Independent graphs for columns 1 and 2, which are [STRAIN]. These both print the growth curve fit summary, and also the growth curve itself with the data points.
    for(i in 0:7){
      gc_fit <- SummarizeGrowth(data$Time, data[,2*j+1+12*i])
      gc_fit2 <- SummarizeGrowth(data$Time, data[,2*j+2+12*i])
      cat("\n\n")
      print(paste(3.2+0.3*i, "pH for ", strain_list[j]))
      print(gc_fit)
      
      cat("\n\n")
      print(paste(5.6+0.3*i, "pH for ", strain_list[j]))
      print(gc_fit2)
      
      
      plot(gc_fit, main = paste(3.2+0.3*i, "pH for ", strain_list[j]))
      plot(gc_fit2, main = paste(5.6+0.3*i, "pH for ", strain_list[j]))
    }
    plot(pH_list, grate_list, ylab = "Growth Rate", xlab = "pH", main = paste(strain_list[j], " pH vs Growth Rate"))
  }
}
```
